85:  - **A 48h window, enforced by the database.** `submitRsvp()` adds `email_sent_at > now() - RSVP_WINDOW_HOURS` to the same UPDATE that records the answer, so the window cannot be beaten by a race or by a stale page left open. Expiry is DERIVED from `email_sent_at`, so there is no stored copy to drift. Unlike the showcase token, an expired RSVP does NOT collapse into a uniform 404: this token guards only a one-bit self-report by the single person it was mailed to, so the (minimal) disclosure that their own link was once valid is worth far less than telling them why they cannot answer. An unknown token stays a uniform failure.
86:  - **Write-once, enforced by the database.** `submitRsvp()` updates `WHERE rsvp_token = ? AND response IS NULL`, so the first answer wins even under a concurrent double submit; there is no read-then-write gap to race. A submit against an answered token reports the standing answer rather than overwriting it.
88:  - **Dual rate limiting.** Per IP (`rsvpLimiter`) on both the resolver and the write, and per token (`rsvpTokenLimiter`) on the write, so a leaked or forwarded link cannot be scripted against the write path. The resolver rate-limits BEFORE any DB work, so it cannot serve as an unthrottled token-validity oracle.

content.content:
- Shows current match status, deadlines, challenge info
- **Event info panel**: an admin-maintained note (Discord link, schedule, venue) shown at
  the top of the hub. Visible to accepted participants even before they are checked in
  (the rest of the hub is gated on check-in). Edited under admin Communications.

### RSVP (`/rsvp/<token>`)
- Purely a headcount signal. An admin presses **Send RSVP Request** on the chapter's
  applications page and every ACCEPTED applicant who has not already been asked gets a
  standalone email with one button. The page behind it offers "Confirm attendance" and
  "I cannot make it"; the answer is logged and nothing else happens.
- Deliberately decoupled from the application workflow: it is NOT part of the acceptance
  email, it never changes `applications.status`, and it has no effect on check-in, teams
  or registration. It exists so organisers can plan catering and venue numbers.
- **The first answer is final.** The lock is enforced in the database (the update is
  conditional on `response IS NULL`), so a double click or a race cannot overwrite it.
  Someone whose plans change is told to reply to the acceptance email.
- **The link expires after 48 hours** (`RSVP_WINDOW_HOURS`), measured from when the
  request was emailed. The deadline is DERIVED from `email_sent_at` rather than stored,
  so the email, the page and the server action always agree; changing the setting moves
  the deadline for links already in flight. Expiry is enforced by the same SQL statement
  that records the answer, so a submit landing just after the deadline cannot slip
  through. An expired link shows a "this window has closed" page rather than a 404: it
  guards only the recipient's own one-bit answer, so telling them why beats hiding that
  their link was ever valid. An answer already given still shows after expiry.
- The answer is recorded ONLY by a POST from a deliberate click. Opening the link writes
  nothing, because mail scanners fetch every URL in an email before the recipient sees it
  and a GET-recorded answer would be filled in by a robot.
- The RSVP token is an unguessable per-application UUID stored in the admin-only
  `application_rsvps` table (never on the `applications` row, which the applicant can
  read). A row exists only once someone has been asked, so pressing the send button twice
  mails nobody twice and newly accepted people are picked up on the next press.
- **One press mails everyone.** There is no fixed chunk: sends run 3 at a time (matching
  the SMTP pool in `lib/email.ts`) under a 45s wall-clock budget. A realistic chapter goes
  out in a single click; a pathologically large one stops cleanly and reports the rest as
  `remaining` to press again, leaving no row behind for anyone it did not reach, so they
  are not silently marked as asked.
- Admin side: the applications page shows a per-row RSVP chip, an RSVP filter, and a
  second row of stat cards (Confirmed / Declined / Awaiting / Not asked) matching the
  status cards above it. "Not asked" counts only status `accepted`, exactly the set the
  send button mails, so it always equals the work one press will clear. Checked-in
  applicants are excluded there (they have arrived and are never sent a request) but
  their earlier answers still count under Confirmed and Declined. CANCELLED applicants
  are excluded from all four counts: they are not coming and that was settled outside
  the RSVP flow, so counting them would leave a never-answering person in "Awaiting" for
  ever and overstate the headcount. Their row is kept, so the record that they were
  asked survives and a later send cannot re-mail them.
- Roles: anyone holding the emailed link can answer it; sending and viewing are available
  to global admins and to that chapter's local admins.

### Check-in (Admin side)
- Admin scans participant QR code at `/admin/check-in`

  the top of the hub. Visible to accepted participants even before they are checked in
  (the rest of the hub is gated on check-in). Edited under admin Communications.

### RSVP (`/rsvp/<token>`)
- Purely a headcount signal. An admin presses **Send RSVP Request** on the chapter's
  applications page and every ACCEPTED applicant who has not already been asked gets a
  standalone email with one button. The page behind it offers "Confirm attendance" and
  "I cannot make it"; the answer is logged and nothing else happens.
- Deliberately decoupled from the application workflow: it is NOT part of the acceptance
  email, it never changes `applications.status`, and it has no effect on check-in, teams
  or registration. It exists so organisers can plan catering and venue numbers.
- **The first answer is final.** The lock is enforced in the database (the update is
  conditional on `response IS NULL`), so a double click or a race cannot overwrite it.
  Someone whose plans change is told to reply to the acceptance email.
- **The link expires after 48 hours** (`RSVP_WINDOW_HOURS`), measured from when the
  request was emailed. The deadline is DERIVED from `email_sent_at` rather than stored,
  so the email, the page and the server action always agree; changing the setting moves
  the deadline for links already in flight. Expiry is enforced by the same SQL statement
  that records the answer, so a submit landing just after the deadline cannot slip
  through. An expired link shows a "this window has closed" page rather than a 404: it
  guards only the recipient's own one-bit answer, so telling them why beats hiding that
  their link was ever valid. An answer already given still shows after expiry.

  nothing, because mail scanners fetch every URL in an email before the recipient sees it
  and a GET-recorded answer would be filled in by a robot.

  `application_rsvps` table (never on the `applications` row, which the applicant can
  read). A row exists only once someone has been asked, so pressing the send button twice
  mails nobody twice and newly accepted people are picked up on the next press.

  the SMTP pool in `lib/email.ts`) under a 45s wall-clock budget. A realistic chapter goes
  out in a single click; a pathologically large one stops cleanly and reports the rest as
  `remaining` to press again, leaving no row behind for anyone it did not reach, so they
  are not silently marked as asked.
- Admin side: the applications page shows a per-row RSVP chip, an RSVP filter, and a
  second row of stat cards (Confirmed / Declined / Awaiting / Not asked) matching the
  status cards above it. "Not asked" counts only status `accepted`, exactly the set the
  send button mails, so it always equals the work one press will clear. Checked-in
  applicants are excluded there (they have arrived and are never sent a request) but
  their earlier answers still count under Confirmed and Declined. CANCELLED applicants
  are excluded from all four counts: they are not coming and that was settled outside
  the RSVP flow, so counting them would leave a never-answering person in "Awaiting" for
  ever and overstate the headcount. Their row is kept, so the record that they were
  asked survives and a later send cannot re-mail them.
- Roles: anyone holding the emailed link can answer it; sending and viewing are available
  to global admins and to that chapter's local admins.

- Admin scans participant QR code at `/admin/check-in`

+  - **A public link never over-promotes.** A `cancelled` application is left untouched (an organiser removed that person deliberately); only `pending`, `waitlisted` and `rejected` are promoted to accepted.

+  - **Consent is explicit.** The page states above the buttons that "I'm in" registers them, confirms attendance and accepts the privacy policy; the optional consents (newsletter, recruiting, media) are copied from their earlier application or left false, never invented.
+  - **Dual rate limiting**, same limiters as the RSVP: per IP on the resolver and the write, per token on the write.

+  - **No token leakage.** The page is `noindex, nofollow, nocache` with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and `finale` is in `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS` (`lib/utils.ts`), so a client-error report carrying the URL is redacted to `/finale/<redacted>` before it reaches the `event_log`.
+  - **Malformed tokens are rejected on shape, before the query**, for the same reason as the RSVP token.

+  - **Sending is GLOBAL admin only.** `sendFinaleInvites()` and `getFinaleInviteBoard()` call `requireAdminAction()`, because the qualifying teams come from the season leaderboard and reach across every chapter, not just one chapter's applicants. The action also refuses any chapter that is not `is_finale`.

- **Loyalty bonus**: `loyalty_bonuses` (migration 00067) holds hand-awarded season bonus points per team. RLS is on with **no policies at all**, so anon and authenticated sessions read zero rows and cannot write; only the service role manages it. The public sees a bonus only through the `leaderboard` view, which runs with its owner's rights (like the view did before) and exposes just the `loyalty_bonus` amount, never the `reason` or `created_at`. Supabase's `security_definer_view` lint flags that view; this is intentional, because switching it to invoker rights would hide published scores and bonuses from public readers.

/**
 * Seed the EPHEMERAL LOCAL Supabase stack (the one started by `supabase start`
 * in CI, or locally for development).
 *
 * This is the local-stack counterpart of scripts/seed-test-via-api.ts. The API
 * script talks to the REMOTE test project over the Management API; this one runs
 * the exact same privileged SQL against the LOCAL Postgres via `psql` (which is
 * preinstalled on the GitHub `ubuntu-latest` runner and ships with the Supabase
 * CLI's local dev workflow). No Management-API token / project ref needed.
 *
 * What it does (mirrors seed-test-via-api.ts):
 *   1. Create the fixed-UUID seed auth.users (profiles FK to auth.users).
 *   2. Clear event_log (append-only trigger disabled around the wipe).
 *   3. Run supabase/seed.sql with the profiles role triggers disabled (the seed
 *      inserts admin/jury/chapter_admin profiles, which prevent_role_on_insert
 *      blocks for non-service_role callers; psql connects as postgres with no
 *      request.jwt.claims, so the trigger must be disabled around the seed).
 *
 * Usage (after `supabase start`):
 *   pnpm exec tsx scripts/seed-local.ts
 *
 * Safety: refuses to run unless the configured Supabase URL is a LOCAL address
 * (127.0.0.1 / localhost). This guarantees it can never touch a remote project.
 * The Postgres connection string is read from `supabase status` (the local
 * stack), never from a remote source.
 */

import { execFileSync } from "child_process";
import { readFileSync } from "fs";
import { resolve } from "path";

const SUPABASE_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL ?? "";

// Hard safety gate: only ever run against a local stack.
if (!/^https?:\/\/(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost)(:|\/|$)/.test(SUPABASE_URL)) {
  console.error(
    `REFUSING: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL (${SUPABASE_URL || "<unset>"}) is not a ` +
      "local address. scripts/seed-local.ts only seeds the local `supabase start` stack."
  );
  process.exit(1);

/**
 * Seed the EPHEMERAL LOCAL Supabase stack (the one started by `supabase start`
 * in CI, or locally for development).
 *
 * This is the local-stack counterpart of scripts/seed-test-via-api.ts. The API
 * script talks to the REMOTE test project over the Management API; this one runs
 * the exact same privileged SQL against the LOCAL Postgres via `psql` (which is
 * preinstalled on the GitHub `ubuntu-latest` runner and ships with the Supabase
 * CLI's local dev workflow). No Management-API token / project ref needed.
 *
 * What it does (mirrors seed-test-via-api.ts):
 *   1. Create the fixed-UUID seed auth.users (profiles FK to auth.users).
 *   2. Clear event_log (append-only trigger disabled around the wipe).
 *   3. Run supabase/seed.sql with the profiles role triggers disabled (the seed
 *      inserts admin/jury/chapter_admin profiles, which prevent_role_on_insert
 *      blocks for non-service_role callers; psql connects as postgres with no
 *      request.jwt.claims, so the trigger must be disabled around the seed).
 *
 * Usage (after `supabase start`):
 *   pnpm exec tsx scripts/seed-local.ts
 *
 * Safety: refuses to run unless the configured Supabase URL is a LOCAL address
 * (127.0.0.1 / localhost). This guarantees it can never touch a remote project.
 * The Postgres connection string is read from `supabase status` (the local
 * stack), never from a remote source.
 */

import { execFileSync } from "child_process";
import { readFileSync } from "fs";
import { resolve } from "path";

const SUPABASE_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL ?? "";

// Hard safety gate: only ever run against a local stack.
if (!/^https?:\/\/(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost)(:|\/|$)/.test(SUPABASE_URL)) {
  console.error(
    `REFUSING: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL (${SUPABASE_URL || "<unset>"}) is not a ` +
      "local address. scripts/seed-local.ts only seeds the local `supabase start` stack."
  );
  process.exit(1);

1	/**
2	 * Query limits to prevent unbounded data fetching.
3	 * All values have sensible defaults well above Season 1 maximums.
4	 *
5	 * Override any limit via environment variable:
6	 *   LIMIT_TEAMS=1000
7	 *   LIMIT_ALL_TEAM_MEMBERS=5000
8	 *   etc.
9	 *
10	 * Set in Vercel Dashboard > Settings > Environment Variables.
11	 * Changes take effect on next function invocation (no redeploy needed).
12	 */
13	
14	function envInt(key: string, fallback: number): number {
15	  const val = process.env[key];
16	  if (!val) return fallback;
17	  const parsed = parseInt(val, 10);
18	  return isNaN(parsed) ? fallback : parsed;
19	}
20	
21	export const QUERY_LIMITS = {
22	  // Teams and their members back the admin Teams page, which is how an operator
23	  // finds a person on an event day. Truncation there is not a degraded view, it
24	  // is a person who appears not to exist, so these sit far above what a single
25	  // season can produce (Season 1 peak: ~60 teams / ~250 members per match) and
26	  // the LimitBanner stays as the never-silent backstop if a deployment ever
27	  // outgrows them.
28	  teams: envInt("LIMIT_TEAMS", 5000),
29	  allTeamMembers: envInt("LIMIT_ALL_TEAM_MEMBERS", 25000),
30	  profiles: envInt("LIMIT_PROFILES", 1000),
31	  // Participants listed on the admin Teams page ("Participants" tab). Separate
32	  // from `profiles` and from `allTeamMembers`: this counts PEOPLE, and the page
33	  // used to cap it with the membership limit, which is a different quantity.
34	  participants: envInt("LIMIT_PARTICIPANTS", 25000),
35	  applicationsPerChapter: envInt("LIMIT_APPLICATIONS_PER_CHAPTER", 2000),
36	  applicationStats: envInt("LIMIT_APPLICATION_STATS", 5000),
37	  screeningScores: envInt("LIMIT_SCREENING_SCORES", 5000),
38	  scores: envInt("LIMIT_SCORES", 1000),
39	  leaderboard: envInt("LIMIT_LEADERBOARD", 500),
40	  // 400: a real event produces 200-300 curated gallery photos (Paris: 223) and
41	  // they render as lazy-loaded w400 thumbnails, so the page stays light.
42	  media: envInt("LIMIT_MEDIA", 400),
43	  submissionsPerChallenge: envInt("LIMIT_SUBMISSIONS_PER_CHALLENGE", 200),
44	  submissionsAll: envInt("LIMIT_SUBMISSIONS_ALL", 1000),
45	  codeReviewsPerChallenge: envInt("LIMIT_CODE_REVIEWS_PER_CHALLENGE", 200),
46	  chapterUnlocks: envInt("LIMIT_CHAPTER_UNLOCKS", 500),
47	  challengeRegistrations: envInt("LIMIT_CHALLENGE_REGISTRATIONS", 500),
48	  // Hard cap for the showcase bulk-CV ZIP. downloadFile makes TWO Drive calls
49	  // per CV (metadata + media) at roughly 1s each, so 100 CVs is ~200s against
50	  // the route's 300s maxDuration: real headroom, not exact-budget roulette.
51	  showcaseCvZip: envInt("LIMIT_SHOWCASE_CV_ZIP", 100),
52	  // Hard cap for the showcase bulk-photo ZIP. Like the CV ZIP, downloadFile
53	  // makes two Drive calls per photo (~1s each); at 150 that is ~300s, matching
54	  // the route's maxDuration. Photos are STORE-zipped (already-compressed JPEGs)
55	  // one at a time, so memory stays flat. A selection larger than this is refused
56	  // loudly before any bytes stream (never a silently truncated album).
57	  showcasePhotoZip: envInt("LIMIT_SHOWCASE_PHOTO_ZIP", 150),
58	  usersLookingForTeam: envInt("LIMIT_USERS_LOOKING_FOR_TEAM", 500),
59	  codeReviewQueueDepth: envInt("LIMIT_CODE_REVIEW_QUEUE_DEPTH", 200),
60	  adminStatsApplications: envInt("LIMIT_ADMIN_STATS_APPLICATIONS", 10000),
61	
62	  // Blocked submission attempts read back for the live admin view. Bounded well
63	  // under PostgREST's 1000-row ceiling on purpose: this is a short rolling
64	  // window (minutes, not the season), and the view reports a count, so the exact
65	  // tail beyond this adds nothing an operator would act on differently.
66	  submissionBlocks: envInt("LIMIT_SUBMISSION_BLOCKS", 500),
67	  applicationNotes: envInt("LIMIT_APPLICATION_NOTES", 500),
68	  // Max recipients fetched per chapter broadcast send. Capped so the synchronous
69	  // send loop stays within the Vercel function timeout (see sendChapterBroadcast,
70	  // which also stops early on a wall-clock budget). Through a 3-connection SMTP
71	  // pool, 200 sends comfortably fit; raise only if your SMTP throughput allows.
72	  broadcastRecipients: envInt("LIMIT_BROADCAST_RECIPIENTS", 200),
73	  broadcasts: envInt("LIMIT_BROADCASTS", 50),
74	};

76	export type QueryLimitKey = keyof typeof QUERY_LIMITS;

78	// Maximum members allowed on a team. A domain invariant (not a query cap):
79	// enforced on registration, invites, joins, and admin overrides. Historically
80	// hardcoded as `5` in lib/actions/teams.ts; centralized here so admin overrides

# NOTE: Supabase env (URL + anon + service-role keys) is NOT set here.
  # The E2E / cross-browser jobs boot their OWN ephemeral local Supabase stack
  # (`supabase start`) per job and export its URL + keys into $GITHUB_ENV, which
  # gives every CI run a fully isolated database so runs can go parallel across
  # branches/PRs (no shared remote test DB). The `checks` job does not need a
  # Supabase connection except for the optional remote migration-applied probe,
  # which sets its own Management-API secrets locally in that job.
  NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL: http://localhost:3001
  NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: 1x00000000000000000000AA
  TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: 1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA
  VERIFICATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ci-test-encryption-key
  ADMIN_EMAIL_DOMAIN: test-ehl.com
  ADMIN_FALLBACK_EMAILS: e2e-admin@test-ehl.com

  GITHUB_TOKEN_EHL: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
  GITHUB_ORG: european-hackathon-league
  # SMTP - optional, registration tests handle missing SMTP gracefully
  SMTP_HOST: ${{ secrets.SMTP_HOST }}
  SMTP_PORT: ${{ secrets.SMTP_PORT }}
  SMTP_USER: ${{ secrets.SMTP_USER }}
  SMTP_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.SMTP_PASSWORD }}

The feature is implemented on branch `feat/finale-invites`, uncommitted and unpushed.

**Everything passes:** typecheck, 1207 unit tests, `pnpm build`, and the E2E suite against a fresh local Supabase (159 passed, 0 failed), including my new invite spec.

**What I built:**
- **Migration `00068_finale_invites.sql`** plus its probe in `scripts/migration-checks.ts`. A `finale_invites` table, admin-only, one invite per person per chapter.
- **`lib/actions/finale-invites.ts`**: the admin send, the read-only token resolver, and the click handler. "I'm in" creates an accepted application (details copied from the person's last application) and sends the acceptance email with the QR code. "I'm out" is only logged.
- **`lib/acceptance-email.ts`**: the acceptance email in one place, now shared by the admin bulk send and the invite click, so they can't drift.
- **`lib/emails/finale-invite.tsx`** with your copy, and `lib/finale.ts` holding the fixed facts (cutoff rank 15, Munich, 10-11 October, RSVP by 30 September).
- **`/finale/<token>`**: the page with the two buttons. It never writes on open, so mail scanners can't accept people.
- **Admin page** under Chapters → Grand Finale → Grand Finale Invites: counters, a per-team list of who answered, and the send button.
- **Tests**: 4 new unit files (39 tests) and an E2E spec. Docs updated in CLAUDE.md, FEATURES, SECURITY and SETUP.

**Three corrections to things I said earlier:**
1. I claimed the local stack booting proved my migration applied. It didn't: the stack restored an old volume. After `supabase db reset` the migration did apply cleanly in strict order.
2. I reported 3 E2E failures as if they might be real. They were my own environment: I'd missed `EMAIL_FAKE_TRANSPORT`, `VERIFICATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and the Turnstile test keys that CI sets. With those, everything passes.
3. My first `pkill` never matched the dev server, so several runs used a stale server. That's what made the jury test look like my fault.

**Two things about your machine:** I stopped your `member-manager` Supabase project to free the port, and it's still stopped. The EHL stack is running; the dev server is stopped. Say the word and I'll restart member-manager.

**Before this can go live** the migration has to be applied to production (`scripts/db-migrate.sh`, then `pnpm db:check`). And since your copy says "top 15" while 19 teams are tied at rank 15 or better, decide whether all 19 get invited: that's what the code does today.

# Get SQL from file or --sql flag
if [ "$1" = "--sql" ]; then
  shift
  SQL="$*"
else
  if [ ! -f "$1" ]; then
    echo "Error: File not found: $1"
    exit 1
  fi
  SQL=$(cat "$1")
fi

echo "SQL to execute:"
echo "$SQL" | head -5
echo "..."
echo ""

run_sql() {
  local ref=$1
  local name=$2
  local result
  result=$(curl -s -X POST "https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/${ref}/database/query" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "$(jq -n --arg q "$SQL" '{query: $q}')")

  if echo "$result" | grep -q '"message"'; then
    echo "FAILED on $name: $result"
    return 1
  else
    echo "OK on $name"
    return 0
  fi
}

echo "Running on Production ($PROD_REF)..."
run_sql "$PROD_REF" "Production"

echo "Running on Test ($TEST_REF)..."
run_sql "$TEST_REF" "Test"

echo ""
echo "Done. Both databases updated."

Both done.

**Draft PR:** https://github.com/tum-ai/ehl/pull/119 (branch `feat/finale-invites`)

**Migration 00068 applied** to production and the test project. `pnpm db:check` confirms all 62 probed migrations are present on both, including `finale_invites`. The change is additive: a new table only, no existing table or row touched.

**On the 19 teams:** the code already invites everyone ranked 15 or better, ties included, so no change was needed. One thing to note: your email copy says "made it into the top 15", which 19 teams will read. Worth a reword if that bothers you, for example "one of the top teams" or "the top 15 places". Tell me and I'll change the one line.

**What's left before invites can go out:**
1. Merge the PR and let it deploy. The admin page and the `/finale/<token>` links only work once the code is live.
2. Check the Grand Finale chapter isn't in `draft` status, or the send button refuses.
3. Publish all scores and any loyalty bonuses first, since the invite list is taken from the leaderboard at the moment you press send.
4. Ask teams to fix their rosters, because only current members get a link.
5. Then: Admin → Chapters → Grand Finale → Grand Finale Invites → **Send invites**.

You also asked earlier for a test copy of the email to your address. I can still do that: say the word and I'll send one using the production SMTP setup, with a placeholder name, team and link.

Your `member-manager` Supabase project is still stopped from the E2E run. Want me to start it again?
